title: 6061-T6 vs T651 vs T6511: Which Temper Do You Actually Need?
summary: T6, T651 and T6511 are the same alloy in three conditions. T651 is stress-relieved plate and cold-finished bar, T6511 is stress-relieved extrusions. Here is which one your print needs and why the minimums differ.
body_markdown:
### What is the difference between 6061-T6 and 6061-T651?


T651 is T6 that has additionally been stress relieved by stretching. Both are solution heat treated and artificially aged to the same strength, but T651 has had residual quench stress relieved, so it holds dimension far better when you machine material off one side. T651 is the normal temper for rolled plate.


### What is the difference between T651 and T6511?


Product form. T651 applies to rolled plate and cold-finished bar, T6511 to extruded bar, rod and shapes with minor straightening permitted after stretching. Both are stress relieved and both carry a 35,000 psi yield minimum, but extruded product has a 38,000 psi ultimate minimum against 42,000 psi for plate and cold-finished bar.


### Is T6511 stronger than T6?


No. They have the same specified strength for a given product form. T6511 adds stress relief, which is about dimensional stability during machining rather than about strength.


### Can I substitute 6061-T6511 bar for a 6061-T651 callout?


Not without checking. They are different product forms with different guaranteed ultimate minimums, 38,000 psi versus 42,000 psi. If the print is yield-driven the substitution is usually harmless, but on a certified job the temper on the cert has to match the print or receiving will reject it.


### Which 6061 temper is best for machining?


Any stress-relieved temper: T651 for plate and cold-finished bar, T6511 for extrusions. Plain T6 without stress relief is the one to avoid for parts with heavy or asymmetric material removal, because the part will move as you cut.
